wikipedia.title: Tuukka Kotti
wikipedia.text:
Tuukka Kotti (born 18 March 1981) is a Finnish professional basketball player for the Tapiolan Honka.
Kotti attended Providence College in the United States, where he played college basketball between 2001 and 2005. He left Finland as a point guard, but gradually turned into a center during his college career.
In 2018, Kotti was named the Korisliiga Most Valuable Player at age 37, while playing with Helsinki Seagulls.

wikipedia.title: Payyanur
wikipedia.text: Payyanur (Malayalam: [pɐjːɐnːuːr]) is a municipal town and a taluk, a sub-district administrative unit, in the Kannur district of Kerala, India. Payyanur is the first municipality in Kerala to establish libraries in all its wards. On 10 March 2018, Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan inaugurated Payyanur as the fifth taluk in the district. Payyanur taluk comprises 22 villages including 16 de-linked from the Taliparamba taluk and six from the Kannur taluk. The town is situated on the banks of the Perumba River.

wikipedia.title: Kandankali
wikipedia.text: Kandankali is a village in Kerala, India. The village is situated about two kilometers south of the town of Payyanur in Kannur district.

wikipedia.title: Kavvayi Backwaters
wikipedia.text:
Kavvayi Backwaters, located near Payyanur, is the third largest backwater in Kerala and the largest one in north Kerala.
The Kavvayi Kayal (backwaters) is dotted with several islands of various size. Valiyaparamba is the largest among them at over 16 square kilometres (6.2 sq mi).

wikipedia.title: Kavvayi Islands
wikipedia.text:
Kavvayi is a group of small islands, near Payyanur in the Kannur district of Kerala. The island is surrounded by Kavvayi Backwaters.
The island of Kavvayi was originally named Kavvil Pattanam. It was renamed as Kavvayi by Sir William Hogan, the then district collector of Hosdurg.

== Do ==

 Poorakkali. Ancient dance festival (updated May 2015)
 Island Walk, Kavvayi Island, Near the Railway Station (3 km). Silent island of the local elites (updated Apr 2015)
 Photography tour by train. Slow trains are called Passenger Trains in India. They are very cheap and punctual. They stop in all small railway stations and give you an opportunity to see the villages from inside and to absorb things slowly. They do not move very slowly, they are only 20% slower than the express trains. Here is a list of railway stations between Payyanur and Kannur where the slow trains will stop: Ezhimala, Payangadi, Kannapuram, Pappinishery, Chirakkal, Kannur. (updated Jun 2015)
 Trekking @ Chandera, Chandera (11 km). Take a slow train ("Passenger Trains") from Payyanur railway station to Chandera railway station.  This is a very rural railway station without any road access.  Only Passenger trains stop here.  The railway station surroundings are very beautiful with paddy fields, banana cultivation and coconut plantations.  You can also access the Valiyaparamba beach from here by boat. (updated Jun 2015)
 Watch Theyyam Dance. Look for select temples during the right season (updated May 2015)
 Visit ancienat family houses, Iruttan Tharavad, Aramana Tharavad, Kandoth (6 km).  (updated Aug 2015)
